interpretation_limits: Input perturbation of a model trained with full state; it is not a retrained stateless baseline or evidence of optimality.
All positions remain on the original fixed-four path; no on-policy consequences or Reader quality are inferred.
Hidden read content can make true-state targets unidentifiable. Retained target acceptance measures information loss, not valid supervision for a new hidden-state task.
Removing fields also shortens inputs and shifts positions; titles/IDs retain prefix and selection information. No length-only or total-state-removal causal claim.
Source-qualified annotations cover only seven targeted source rows, including masks, not a representative noise-rate sample.
No independent generalization, confidence calibration, learned stopping utility or whole-pipeline net benefit is established.

source_review_notes.finding: Full input declares sufficient after reading birthplace-only biography; source-qualified target is pool exhaustion. Removing read text changes these to exhausted. This label improvement does not prove a hidden-state policy can reason correctly.
Needed open_p4 is never selected by any view. At step1 a STOP-to-open change still chooses an unrelated premise; at later steps all views remain incorrectly sufficient.
Full and titles-only choose sufficient; IDs-only loses that judgment and chooses exhausted. Sensitivity can also remove a correct decision.

Prior QA gain cases also vary inconsistently; titles-only selects the Lana supplement at step1, IDs-only stops, and all views prematurely stop after the film/director evidence. These examples were not added to the predeclared source-qualified aggregate.

decision: Frozen model responds strongly to read-content perturbations, but available source-qualified prefixes do not establish reliable state use or a quality advantage for full inputs. Do not deploy omission, retrain on dev, or infer QA/net savings from this probe. Source-qualified learning and matched trained/on-policy controls remain open.
